title: AVOID this Meta Ads Tactic
transcript: What's the popular meta-adds tactic that you think is overrated? Horizontal scaling. And what I mean by that is, someone will have a campaign, a meta-add campaign's performing well, and they will duplicate it and run an identical copy or something very similar alongside the original. And they might do this multiple times thinking, okay, well, I've got $100 a day spent in one campaign, I'll spend another $100, another $100, another. Meta really doesn't like that. You end up with auction overlap. The campaign's compete meta isn't able to work out the correct delivery of ad impressions to certain individuals if they're spread across multiple campaigns. So I much prefer vertical scaling where you scale the existing ad campaign budget instead of fragmenting everything with horizontal scaling.
